experiment: Phase B1 - converged strong end-to-end LM baseline on real Corr2Cause

train_subset.note: first 20000 rows of corr2cause train after a seed-0 shuffle

eval.note: splits byte-identical to the GNN/ceiling comparison; perturb/evaluate/f1 reused from causal_corr2cause_learned.py

config.loss: class-weighted CrossEntropy (pos upweighted by neg/pos ratio)
config.memory_note: gradient checkpointing + gradient accumulation (micro-batch 4 -> effective 8) keep gradients EXACT while cutting peak RAM ~6.5GB -> ~3GB; distilbert is LayerNorm-only so micro-batching is mathematically equivalent
config.provenance: epoch 1 trained on GPU (batch 8) before the GPU thermally wedged; epochs continued on CPU at the same effective batch 8 via checkpoint resume. Effective training = 2 epochs, effective batch 8. A clean from-scratch re-run reproduces (CPU nondeterminism aside).

finding: The decoupling win is NOT 'OOD-only': the decoupled GNN beats a CONVERGED distilbert even i.i.d. (0.927 vs 0.523), and the LM is not relabel-invariant - it collapses under variable renaming (0.523 -> 0.154) and gets WORSE with training (epoch-1 relabel 0.292 -> epoch-2 0.154), i.e. it learns lexical/letter shortcuts rather than the causal structure. Complementary failure modes: the LM is paraphrase-robust but relabel-fragile, while the regex->GNN is relabel-robust but paraphrase-fragile.
caveat: distilbert is 66M params. Jin et al. (2024) report larger fine-tuned LMs (e.g. RoBERTa-large) reaching higher i.i.d. F1 (~0.8) but exhibiting the same OOD collapse. So a real fine-tune at this scale does not approach 0.6 i.i.d.; the 'strong LM ties i.i.d.' claim holds only for much larger models, which this box cannot train.

reproduce.from_scratch_2ep: DEVICE=cpu NT=6 EFF_BATCH=8 MICRO=4 GC=1 STEPS=5000 SAVE_EVERY=1000 EVAL_AT_END=1 uv run --extra torch --with datasets --with transformers python examples/causal_corr2cause_b1_lm.py
